revenue: Net sales rose $1,076M (+9.6%; +9.2% constant currency) for the six months, with growth across every operating segment — Commercial +9.4%, Government +9.6%, Education +1.5% and UK/Canada 'Other' +20.4%. Growth was demand-driven, concentrated in data storage and servers, notebooks/mobile devices, software and netcomm, on an identical 127 selling days, so this was volume rather than calendar or FX benefit (FX was actually a slight prior-year tailwind that reversed).
gross_profit: Gross profit grew only 6.2% versus 9.6% sales growth because gross margin compressed 60bps to 20.5%, driven by mix shift into lower-margin hardware categories (and lower margin within those categories). Government was the weak spot at -290bps to 19.5% on hardware and services mix; Commercial fell 50bps and Other 110bps, only partly offset by Education's +90bps and, in Q2, a higher contribution of netted-down revenue.
operating_income: Operating margin slipped from 7.0% to 6.6% as the gross margin squeeze was compounded by selling and administrative expenses rising 7.8% ($123M) on higher compensation, including performance-based incentives, and workplace optimization costs. Unallocated Headquarters costs widened $30M, and the $44M of workplace optimization charges (vs $13M a year ago) explain much of the gap — non-GAAP operating income still grew 4.6%.
interest_expense: Interest expense, net rose only $2M (1.4%) for the six months, attributed to higher average borrowings under the senior unsecured revolving loan facility. The new product financing arrangement entered in Q2 2026 also carries contractual financing costs recognized as interest expense, though the filing does not quantify that impact.
pre_tax: Pre-tax income grew 3.4% to $692M, well behind the 9.6% sales increase, so pre-tax margin narrowed roughly 40bps — essentially the same gross margin mix pressure and higher compensation/workplace optimization costs that hit operating income, with modestly higher net interest adding a small further drag. (Reported net income growth was further muted by the effective tax rate rising to 26.3% from 25.8% on equity-comp tax shortfalls.)
current_assets: The filing does not present a current ratio, but the working capital build is clear: accounts receivable consumed $1,054M and inventory $418M in the first half (versus $450M and $147M a year ago), funded largely by a $896M increase in trade payables and revolver draws, while cash fell $256M. The cash conversion cycle lengthened to 21 days from 16, with DSO up to 93 days on collection timing and the shift to multi-year software purchases, and DIO up to 16 days on customer stocking and higher hardware costs.
total_debt: Total unsecured indebtedness stood at $5.8 billion at June 30, 2026, with $1.7 billion of revolver availability remaining and full covenant compliance. The increase reflects incremental drawings on the Revolving Loan Facility in 2026 — used to fund working capital growth and $545M of share repurchases — in contrast to prior-year long-term debt repayment.
operating_cash: Operating cash flow fell $223M to $220M despite higher net income, as working capital absorbed cash: receivables (timing of collections plus higher sales) and inventory (customer stocking and higher hardware costs) were a far larger drag than in 2025, only partly offset by a $512M larger build in trade payables. Free cash flow dropped to $166M and adjusted free cash flow to $278M from $459M, a meaningful reduction in internally generated coverage relative to the dividend and buyback program.
